security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel KVM, when a guest VM with vsstatus.ACES≠Off executes ACE instructions (V=1), if the host hypervisor's mstatus.ACES=Off (the default for hosts not using ACE), the hardware raises illegal-instruction exceptions on all guest ACE instructions because the new spec requires BOTH mstatus.ACES and vsstatus.ACES to be non-Off — unlike FS/VS where only the virtualized status field controls trapping. The KVM hypervisor must explicitly set mstatus.ACES to a non-Off value before entering a guest that uses ACE, or the guest's ACE functionality is silently broken.
security_spec.summary: Dual ACES gate in V=1 mode (both mstatus.ACES and vsstatus.ACES must be non-Off) diverges from standard FS/VS virtualization semantics where only the virtualized status controls trapping; KVM must explicitly manage host mstatus.ACES for guest ACE support

findings.finding: ACE/ACES extension is not implemented in this kernel. kvm_arch_vcpu_load() writes guest vsstatus via csr_write(CSR_VSSTATUS, ...) but never reads, writes, or modifies mstatus. The CSR bit definitions in arch/riscv/include/asm/csr.h contain no SR_ACES or ACE-related bits. Consequently, there is no code to set mstatus.ACES to a non-Off value before entering a guest that uses ACE. If ACE support were added, this function would need to ensure the host mstatus.ACES field is non-Off before VCPU entry, since the ACE spec requires both mstatus.ACES and vsstatus.ACES to be non-Off to avoid illegal-instruction traps on guest ACE instructions.

This inline function swaps host/guest scounteren, senvcfg, and optionally sstateen0 CSRs before guest entry, following the standard pattern for other extension state (FS, VS, SMSTATEEN). There is no corresponding swap for mstatus.ACES. The architectural risk is that mstatus is a machine-mode CSR in HS-mode systems, and unlike sstatus/vsstatus which have hardware virtualization support, mstatus bits like ACES would require explicit save/restore by the hypervisor — a pattern that does not yet exist in this codebase.

The assembly world-switch saves and restores only supervisor-level CSRs (sstatus, stvec, sscratch, sepc) via csrrw instructions. mstatus is never touched. The host hypervisor's mstatus — including any future ACES field — persists unchanged across guest entry/exit. In the standard RISC-V H-extension design, mstatus is not virtualized by hardware (unlike sstatus which is swapped with vsstatus on V=1 transitions), so any mstatus.ACES manipulation would need to be done explicitly by the hypervisor before sret into the guest.
findings.snippet:
csrrw   t0, CSR_SSTATUS, t0       /* sstatus only, not mstatus */
csrrw   t1, CSR_STVEC, t1
csrw    CSR_SEPC, t2
csrrw   t3, CSR_SSCRATCH, a0

findings.finding: The status register (sstatus/mstatus) bit definitions include SR_FS (bits 13:14), SR_VS (bits 9:10), and SR_XS (bits 15:16) following the standard Off/Initial/Clean/Dirty model, but no SR_ACES definition exists. The ACE extension's status field encoding is not present in this kernel. This is consistent with the ACE ISA extension not yet being ratified or merged into the mainline kernel.
findings.snippet:
#define SR_FS           _AC(0x00006000, UL)
#define SR_FS_OFF       _AC(0x00000000, UL)
#define SR_VS           _AC(0x00000600, UL)
#define SR_VS_OFF       _AC(0x00000000, UL)
// No SR_ACES, SR_ACES_OFF, etc.
